implementation_choice.text: EVAS convention, not an LRM rule (events.md:1269-1276 at d6b7543f; standard-line decision item SL-DEC-20261028-01, recommendation A, awaiting the coordinator): an exact zero belongs to the arriving segment. A guard pair (a, 0) with a nonzero fires once in direction -sign(a), filtered by dir, whether or not a next segment exists; this covers isolated zeros, zero-plateau entry and stop. Zero to zero and zero to nonzero do not fire; an initial zero plateau and an all-zero input do not fire. LRM 5.10.3.1 and 5.10.3.2 do not define these four degenerate cases.

EVAS executes timer-triggered bodies, including an OR body fired by its timer leaf at the same instant as a cross, at the exact scheduled time and compares point values (events.md:1835-1838). This is the expected value for this batch; it is not a cross-backend tie answer, because a simulator placing the point just beyond the time may decide an exactly-at-threshold comparison the other way.

Documented EVAS contract (events.md@d6b7543f #cross-right-limit): read te=tau+; a comparison exactly zero at tau needs a post-root certificate: (1) fired leaf with an exact same zero set d=k*g, sign(k)*s with s the PWL side (segment end sign; at a knot the next segment; a zero end value is a proven plateau); (2) other stateless conditions: derivative enclosure of the accepted history on [lo, next_up(hi)] strictly signed, or exactly [0,0] (plateau); (3) right window W=[lo, next_up(hi)]: plateau (first-order dependence exactly zero on W, e.g. constant inputs, exact cancellation q=V(w); V(w)-q, floor/real-to-integer only when all of W lies in one bin) or a window enclosure that already decides the comparison.
Without a certificate return kernel event_condition; continue only when both arms behave identically. Loop conditions use the same rule (while loops are unrolled into guarded trips).
Time-invariant equalities keep their value (the difference reads no input or operator column and no state assigned in this body from a voltage or history).

Timer-triggered bodies, including an OR body fired by its timer leaf at the same instant as a cross, run at the exact time; an unrelated same-instant timer does not change a cross body's reads; a cross-triggered body in a batch that also contains a separate timer block uses only conditions without operator columns (this restriction does not apply to an OR body fired by its own timer leaf); paid history contexts install only the leaf side and charge right-window reads to the same ledger; budget/resource/IR errors are reported as such, not as missing certificates.

Known limit: assigned values use the tau root box (the right limit for continuous quantities); floor/rounding arguments exactly on a breakpoint at tau assign the tau value, so only exactly-zero comparisons are protected. Ordinary contribution Selects are continuous-time expressions and keep the g(tau)=0 decision.

lrm_mandated.text: A cross-triggered body observes the post-crossing side: with exact PWL ramps, V(code)>=1.5 after a falling crossing of 1.5 is false and V(u)>0.5 after a rising crossing of 0.5 is true.

A timer event occurs at a time point within time_tol of its scheduled time; without time_tol the point is at, or just beyond, that time (5.10.3.3). The LRM therefore does not fix a unique branch when a timer-body comparison is exactly at its threshold at the scheduled time.
cross() generates no event at t=0 (5.10.3.2).

must_not.text: Return the value at tau (g(tau)=0 treated as equality) without a diagnostic: observed on d6b7543f for single leaf, falling-only leaf, two and three OR leaves, ternary, if/else, integer and real targets, rising with strict >, and cross OR a non-coincident timer.
Choose a branch by a nominal or rounded sample when no certificate exists.

source_fields.budget: Exact for counts (integer equality) and messages (pattern match). Values on the 120001-row stateless-gain grid are within 1e-12 V (input) and 3e-12 V (output) of the closed form, compared with Fractions. The dynamic RC check holds every one of its 120001 rows to the request's own accuracy: |y - (1 - exp(-t))| <= absolute_V + relative*|y| with exp in 50-digit Decimal, where absolute_V = 1e-12 V and relative = 1e-10 are the SCS defaults (the deck has no options line) echoed in effective_controls; the certified voltage_bounds_V contain 1 - exp(-t) and their half-width is within the same tolerance. Discovery does not collect that check: CI runs it by name in the rust-regression job on every regression selection, with or without package, on a release kernel through scripts/run_explicit_checks.py, which fails unless it ran exactly once and passed, and the CI inventory records the step as a CI by-name check entry. A local run of that step is recorded in evas/capabilities/observations/capability-batch1-20261028/pr-evidence/rc-check-release.json in the capability batch 1 construction archive, sha256 e86536dbfb230d46195e61b18d1cdfba8f73620c43fd6cf395b6503c3f526c3f.
allowed_behavior: One limit of 1000000 points at the eight Python checkpoints (SCS grid, rows after including source corners, saved rows with forced points, pulse corners, explicit, periodic and combined strobe tables, response strobe_evidence.times) and at the kernel's strobetimes count; the Python and Rust constants are equal.
A count within the limit is admitted; one more is rejected and the message names the limit in force, for example "output point budget (1000000) exceeded".
The SCS grid is admitted while floor(stop/maxstep) + 2 <= limit; an exactly divisible stop/maxstep needs only floor + 1 rows, so admission is conservative by one row.
Counts above the former 100000 boundary are admitted; unrelated budgets that share the number 100000 (netlist tokens, integer invariants, native audit) are unchanged.
The limit changes admission only; admitted requests compute the same results as before.

source_fields.budget: Exact for every control fact: echo, error kind, limit in the message, ledger slots and request bytes compare by equality, and the C8 comparison requires the echoed default as the integer 1000000000 before removing it. Raising the limit changes no numerical result: unset and explicit default give byte-identical responses; simulate_scs at 2e12 saves data equal to the default run; as one-time PR evidence and not a CI test, the default response through a kernel built from main d6b7543f equals the previous kernel's after removing only the echo key (receipt evas/capabilities/observations/capability-batch1-20261028/pr-evidence/main-kernel-checks-r3-final.json in the capability batch 1 construction archive, sha256 bf95d3f3cd876a6e072f4789678869aae25d71e15dbfea38cd2ef3a3636e50e5). Completed rows of the slew request are within the request's own tolerance absolute_V + relative*|y| read from effective_controls, which must equal the requested 1e-12 V and 0; rows are compared with Fractions. Exhaustion depends on the request bytes, because the ledger charges serialized program text: the two end-to-end tests name their source proof_limit.va, so the checkout path never enters their requests. Measured total work is 891444759 for 1000 rows (108555241 below 1e9, 841444759 above 5e7) and 2669543465 for 3000 rows (1669543465 above 1e9, 7330456535 below 1e10); each extra character of the source name adds 11061 and 33061 work, so the tightest margin, 1000 rows under 1e9, allows 9814 more characters. No universal tolerance is introduced.
allowed_behavior: Unset: the request ledger is [128, 8192, 1000000000], the request bytes are those of the previous release (the field is not sent) and the response echoes effective_controls.proof_work_limit = 1000000000.

Set to an integer N with 1 <= N <= 10000000000000: N is the work slot of every source-transition proof ledger the request builds, with one exception. Slots 0 and 1, the sharing between consumers and the no-refund rule for failed reservations are unchanged, and each ledger is sticky. A consumer shares a bound owner's ledger (source context, procedure, analytic sources) and otherwise builds its own from the same N, so one request can hold several: measured, the slew and RC requests hold the events ledger [128, 8192, N] and the operator-plan ledger [8192, 8192, N], and an analytic-source request holds the request ledger and the events ledger, both [128, 8192, N]. The exception is the transition-input form audit (operators.rs, transition_input): each call builds a fresh default ledger [128, 8192, 1000000000] that does not take N. The kernel admits at most 100000 IR values with container depth 96, which bounds one audit at about 6.9e6 work (measured at most 540847), so that ledger never binds.

Every other value is rejected by the layer that receives it. In a kernel request, 0, above 1e13, negative, any float including 2e12 and 2000000000000.0, bool, string, JSON null and an integer beyond u64 are invalid_inputs. In a CLI manifest a present transient.proof_work_limit must be an integer in range: null and every other shape are rejected while the manifest is read (manifest_input, naming the field), before anything is sent, and omitting the field is the default. The CLI flag accepts decimal digits only, and only for transient and simulate. In the Python API None is the default and means unset (the request bytes are those of the unset request above); any other non-integer or out-of-range value raises ValueError before sending.
Exhaustion reports step_budget with the limit in force ("exceeds N").
The limit is request metadata, not part of the serialized config identity: a request that completes under two limits is charged the same work and returns the same values.

A kernel without the field rejects it as invalid_request (fail closed); request_protocol_version stays null. This was checked once against a kernel built from main d6b7543f before the field existed, as one-time PR evidence and not a CI test (receipt evas/capabilities/observations/capability-batch1-20261028/pr-evidence/main-kernel-checks-r3-final.json in the capability batch 1 construction archive, sha256 bf95d3f3cd876a6e072f4789678869aae25d71e15dbfea38cd2ef3a3636e50e5). Under CI, test_kernel_rejects_an_unknown_transient_field_by_name keeps the same rule for any unknown transient field.

source_fields.normative_basis: No clause of LRM 2.4 or LRM 2023 defines a proof-work budget. The limit is an EVAS request contract and implementation budget recorded in evas/docs/reference/proof-work-limit.md; it is neither a correctness criterion nor a performance promise.

related_source_locations.relation: The LRM leaves the numerical method and its effort to the simulator ("There are a number of different approaches to solving this problem numerically"); it sets no work budget.

target_scope_applicability.analysis: transient requests only; the static solve path keeps its fixed default ledger and has no request field
target_scope_applicability.statement: Applies to every transient request EVAS admits in the voltage-domain target. It admits no construct and no model outside the target: general-current-kcl, mixed-digital-ams, noise-ac-pss-rf, general-multistability and vpi stay excluded, and fine-grained clause membership stays pending.
